title: Exceptional internal Hom versus exceptional pullback
statement:
Fix the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, and let $c:C\to Z$ be a separated
finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes which is admissible at
$A$ ([def-trf-admissibility]). For
$M,N\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ the canonical comparison

$$
R\mathcal Hom_A\bigl(c^*M,c^!N\bigr)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
c^!R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N)
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in $M$ and $N$. Its first variable is
required to be an ordinary pullback and its second an exceptional one;
the analogous statement with $c^!$ in the first variable is false.

proof.text:
Work at the fixed finite coefficient stage of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Write $\mathcal D_T=D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$, $F=Rc_!$, $G=Rc^!$, and $L=Lc^*$. The admissibility assumption [def-trf-admissibility] specifies $F:\mathcal D_C	o\mathcal D_Z$, $G:\mathcal D_Z	o\mathcal D_C$ and $F\dashv G$, including its counit $\epsilon$. The statement allows $C$ and $Z$ to be arbitrary finite-type $k$-schemes (only $c$ is assumed separated), so the domain checks use preservation results without a separatedness hypothesis on the schemes. Ordinary pullback: [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] applies to the separated finite-type morphism $c$ of finite-type $k$-schemes and gives $LM\in\mathcal D_C$. Derived tensor: [lem-sf-tensor-ctf](ii) on the finite-type schemes $C$ and $Z$ gives $P\otimes_A^L LM\in\mathcal D_C$ for every $P\in\mathcal D_C$ and $FP\otimes_A^L M\in\mathcal D_Z$ (using $FP\in\mathcal D_Z$). Derived internal Hom on a finite-type $k$-scheme $T$, for $K,K_1\in\mathcal D_T$ with Tor amplitudes $[a,b]$ and $[c',d']$: by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii) there are bounded constructible etale complexes $K',K_1'$ with $K\cong
u_T^*K'$ and $K_1\cong
u_T^*K_1'$; by [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii) they have finite Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ and $[c',d']$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$. Since $T$ has finite dimension [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], choose an integer $m\geq0$ with $\dim T\leq m$; then [thm-sf-hom-ctf] puts $R\mathcal Hom_A(K',K_1')$ in $D^b_{ctf}(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](i) puts $
u_T^*R\mathcal Hom_A(K',K_1')$ in $\mathcal D_T$, and [thm-sf-hom-comparison-constructible] identifies the latter with $R\mathcal Hom_A(
u_T^*K',
u_T^*K_1')\cong R\mathcal Hom_A(K,K_1)$. As $\mathcal D_T$ is defined by conditions on cohomology sheaves, it is closed under isomorphism, so $R\mathcal Hom_A(K,K_1)\in\mathcal D_T$. Applied on $Z$ to $(M,N)$ and on $C$ to $(LM,GN)$, this places $R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N)$, $H=R\mathcal Hom_A(LM,GN)$ and $J=GR\mathcal Hom_A(M,N)$ in their indicated categories. Thus every exceptional-adjunction instance below is on its specified constructible domain; no ambient exceptional adjoint is used.

source.place: Complete adjunction/projection-formula calculation, followed by representability and naturality

proof.text:
For any of the small ringed sites $(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A_T)$, abbreviate derived internal Hom to $H_T(-,-)$. The first assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], followed by degree-zero global sections and [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] on each side, gives the natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_T(U,H_T(V,W))\cong H^0(T,H_T(U,H_T(V,W)))\cong H^0(T,H_T(U\otimes_A^L V,W))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(U\otimes_A^L V,W).$$
This is precisely the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction for the concrete derived Hom in the statement. Since the constructible categories are full, the same bijection applies to their objects. This derives the required adjunction from statements that actually assert the relevant facts, rather than assuming it from the definition of the operations.

For $P\in\mathcal D_C$, compose the adjunction of step 2, the specified exceptional adjunction [def-trf-admissibility], the projection isomorphism [fix-prop-projection-formula] at $(c,P,M)$, and then the two adjunctions in reverse order:
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_C(P,H)&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_C(P\otimes_A^L LM,GN)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(F(P\otimes_A^L LM),N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(FP\otimes_A^L M,N)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(FP,R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N))\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_C(P,J).
\end{aligned}$$
The middle bijection sends $b:F(P\otimes_A^L LM)\to N$ to $b\circ\operatorname{PF}_{c,P,M}$, where $\operatorname{PF}_{c,P,M}:FP\otimes_A^L M\xrightarrow{\sim}F(P\otimes_A^L LM)$. Its hypotheses hold: $P$ is bounded constructible and $M$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Denote the composite by $\Phi_P$. Each constituent is natural in $P$, contravariantly in $M$ and covariantly in $N$, so the composite has those naturalities.

source.place: Complete adjunction/projection-formula calculation, followed by representability and naturality

proof.text: Here is the representability argument explicitly, inside $\mathcal D_C$. Let $\Psi_P=\Phi_P^{-1}$, put $h=\Phi_H(1_H):H\to J$ and $u=\Psi_J(1_J):J\to H$. Naturality gives $\Phi_P(a)=h\circ a$ for every $a:P\to H$, by applying naturality to $a$ and $1_H$. Likewise $\Psi_P(b)=u\circ b$. Taking $a=u$ and $b=h$, the inverse-bijection identities give $h\circ u=1_J$ and $u\circ h=1_H$. Thus $h$ is an isomorphism. This also proves uniqueness of the arrow inducing the displayed Hom bijections, without applying a scheme-specific version of Yoneda to a derived category.

source.place: Complete adjunction/projection-formula calculation, followed by representability and naturality

proof.text:
Identify $h$ with the canonical comparison, rather than just an unspecified isomorphism. Write $\mathrm{ev}:H\otimes_A^L LM\to GN$ for the tensor–Hom adjunct of $1_H$. Unwinding $\Phi_H(1_H)$ in step 3 shows that $h$ is the result of transposing the following map first by tensor–Hom on $Z$, then by $F\dashv G$:
$$FH\otimes_A^L M\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}_{c,H,M}}F(H\otimes_A^L LM)\xrightarrow{F(\mathrm{ev})}FGN\xrightarrow{\epsilon_N}N.$$
This is the canonical comparison specified by evaluation, projection and exceptional adjunction. All these maps have the domains verified in step 1. For $a:M'\to M$ and $b:N\to N'$, let $H(a,b):H(M,N)\to H(M',N')$ and $J(a,b):J(M,N)\to J(M',N')$ be the induced maps. Naturality of the Hom bijections in step 3, evaluated at $1_{H(M,N)}$, gives
$$J(a,b)\circ h_{M,N}=\Phi^{M',N'}_{H(M,N)}(H(a,b))=h_{M',N'}\circ H(a,b).$$
This is the asserted naturality in both variables.

source.place: Complete adjunction/projection-formula calculation, followed by representability and naturality

proof.text:
For the warning about the first variable, take $c:\mathbf A^1_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $M=N=A$ in degree zero. The smooth purity theorem [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] gives $c^!A=A(1)[2]$. The twist is a locally free rank-one coefficient sheaf by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free]. Restriction to a trivializing object commutes with derived internal Hom by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. On that slice site, the K-injective Hom definition [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] computes $R\mathcal Hom_A(A,A)$ as $\mathcal Hom_A(A,I^\bullet)=I^\bullet$ for a resolution $A\to I^\bullet$, hence as $A$. Thus the global scalar-action map $A\to R\mathcal Hom_A(A(1),A(1))$ restricts to a quasi-isomorphism on every trivializing object: its cone has zero cohomology locally, hence zero cohomology sheaves by the sheaf axiom. It is therefore a quasi-isomorphism globally, so $R\mathcal Hom_A(A(1),A(1))\cong A$. Cancelling the equal shifts in the two Hom variables, as allowed by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], gives
$$R\mathcal Hom_A(c^!A,c^!A)\cong A,\qquad c^!R\mathcal Hom_A(A,A)\cong A(1)[2].$$
These are not isomorphic: their only nonzero cohomology sheaves lie in degrees $0$ and $-2$, respectively, using the cochain shift convention [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The coefficient ring $A_{E,n}$ is nonzero for $n\geq1$. Thus replacing the ordinary first pullback by an exceptional one fails even for this smooth admissible morphism.

source.place: Final warning about exceptional pullback in the first variable; explicit affine-line counterexample using the lecture-notes smooth-purity route

split_report.summary: N3 expanded the finite-coefficient adjunction/projection-formula proof into six steps, including a domain check, an explicit derivation of tensor-Hom adjunction from existing ringed-site results, inverse representability maps, the evaluation/counit formula identifying the canonical comparison, both-variable naturality, and the affine-line counterexample to the exceptional-first-variable variant. No new nodes. Removed only the stale claim that the warning is recorded in the admissibility definition; the mathematical statement and coefficient conventions are unchanged.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the five Hom-set bijections, the projection-formula sentence, and the Yoneda/naturality conclusion of the current main-20261015 proof of lem-trf-exceptional-internal-hom-exchange; also justifies its statement's final warning. The sk-d-trace-class unit remains the supported diagonal trace-class construction; this auxiliary exchange is proved by its existing formal route.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N3-20af83521 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, all 6 steps, every cited statement, the main-20261015 and master sources, unit sk-d-trace-class and chapter sec-trace-formula, Stacks 08J9/08JA (sites-cohomology.tex:8874-8910), and the three citers. The statement matches the source. Only the stale words 'as recorded in [def-trf-admissibility]' were removed, which is correct because the current admissibility node has no such warning. No hypothesis was weakened, and the coefficient category stays A_{E,n} on the pro-etale site with D^b_ctf. One fault (E1): step 1 cited thm-sf-ctf-stability, which assumes separated schemes, by appealing to a 'standing separated setting'. The item only says C and Z are finite-type k-schemes, and the admissibility definition allows a non-separated target. I fixed step 1 to use nodes that need no separatedness: lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude (Lc^*), lem-sf-tensor-ctf(ii) (tensor), and for Hom the etale-origin transfer through lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin(ii), lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude(ii)/(i), lem-kun-dimension-finite-type, thm-sf-hom-ctf and thm-sf-hom-comparison-constructible. proof_deps and split_report.tool_uses were updated to match, and the thm-sf-ctf-stability entry was removed. Steps 2-6 verified: (2) the ringed-site currying lemma plus H^0=Hom gives tensor-Hom; (3) fix-prop-projection-formula is in the correct direction and needs no separatedness of X or Y; (4) the Yoneda inverse identities hold; (5) evaluation, projection and counit give the canonical map, natural in both variables; (6) the A^1 counterexample gives degree 0 against degree -2, nonzero, using lecture-notes purity and no SGA. There are no new nodes and no duplicates (the tensor-adjunction nodes state a different exchange). Dependency walk found no cycle.
